articles.headline: Masthead and corresponding editors
articles.summary: Christian Recorder, Vol. VII No. 18, Philadelphia, Saturday May 4, 1867. Masthead: Rev. Elisha Weaver, Publisher, General Book Steward, No. 631 Pine Street. Corresponding editors: Baltimore Conference Rev. B. T. Tanner; Philadelphia Conference A. L. Stanford; New York L. Patterson; New England W. W. Grimes; Ohio Samuel Watts; Indiana McIntosh; Missouri M. M. Clark; California T. M. D. Ward.

articles.headline: Baltimore Annual Conference, fiftieth session (report)
articles.author: W. D. Harris
articles.summary: Report of the 50th session of the Baltimore Conference of the A.M.E. Church, Bishop Wayman presiding with Bishop Payne. Business included a Virginia provisional conference (J. M. Brown), B. T. Tanner's manuscript 'Apology for African Methodism', admission of candidates and probationers. Rev. Elisha Weaver, General Book Steward, read his report on the Book Concern and the Recorder. At the Missionary Anniversary speakers included Maj. Gen. Gregory, James Lynch (editor of the Recorder), the bishops, Corresponding Secretary Rev. John M. Brown, Rev. A. T. Carr of the South Carolina Conference, Rev. H. M. Turner (Georgia) and Rev. Mr. Woodlin of Brooklyn. Baltimore candidates and probationers (T. M. Cole, W. Derrick, P. Shephard, J. H. Spriggs, J. F. Sisson, A. Woodhouse and others) are text only.

articles.headline: Men of the Times
articles.author: Louis Stanton Day [VERIFY]
articles.summary: For the Christian Recorder. An address in praise of the 'men of the times' (Garrison, Lincoln and others). Non-local, devotional/political essay; signed Louis Stanton Day [VERIFY signature].

articles.headline: Bethel Church Parsonage
articles.author: Progress [VERIFY pseudonym]
articles.summary: For the Christian Recorder. The members of Bethel have taken up collections for a parsonage; the writer asks whether it would not be best to build the parsonage on the ground adjacent to the church. This ground belongs to the Corporation though leased upon ground rent to other parties. The lot running 72 feet east from the north-east corner of 6th and Lombard St. has not paid the church one cent of ground rent for eight or ten years. The church surroundings are a disgrace: old frame shanties; on the corner of 6th and Lombard the tavern is never closed; in the yard of the shanty next to the church a swing kept for hire, used on the Sabbath by lads who annoy the Sabbath-school. Urges the Corporation to repossess the ground and erect a handsome parsonage.

articles.headline: Editorial items: New church in Philadelphia; colored voters of New Jersey; Mrs. Harper; Sarah's Tent
articles.summary: Items: the M.E. preachers' meeting of Philadelphia considered a new (John Wesley, colored M.E.) church; a lot costing $3,500 with $2,700 needed. D. D. Butler of Camden presented a memorial to the N.J. legislature on behalf of 7,000 colored voters. Mrs. F. E. W. Harper lecturing at Charleston S.C. on 'The Colored Man as a Social and Political Force'. Rev. James B. Reeve(s) of Central Presbyterian called to the 15th Street Presbyterian Church, Washington.
people: of Camden, memorial to N.J. legislature
pastor, Central Presbyterian Church (Rev.) [printed Reeves; elsewhere J. B. Reeve]

articles.headline: Book notice: William Still's pamphlet on the city railway cars
articles.summary: Notice of William Still's pamphlet 'A Brief Narrative of the Struggle for the Rights of the Colored People of Philadelphia in the City Railway Cars', refuting slanders on the 'Car Question'. (Streetcar topic.)

articles.headline: Conference schedule: Philadelphia Annual Conference
articles.summary: The Philadelphia Conference to meet in Philadelphia, May 18th, Bishop Wayman presiding (from the published schedule of conferences).

articles.headline: Information wanted: Elizabeth Parrott; James Watson
articles.summary: Information wanted of Elizabeth Parrott, wife of Nelson Parrott [also printed Parrett], formerly of a Virginia court house town; address Nelson Parrett, care of Rev. Jacob M. Mitchell, 613 Lombard st., Philadelphia (Apr 20-4t). Also of James Watson, who left Philadelphia in 1861 and shipped from Boston in the ship Lydia Scofield; his mother Jane N. Watson, Chester, Delaware Co., Pa., care of William Murphy (apr13-4t). Other information-wanted notices (Kentucky, Wilmington N.C., Millville N.J., Milton N.C.) are text only.

articles.headline: Marriages
articles.summary: April 25, by Rev. Jacob M. Mitchell, Mr. William C. Hooper to Mrs. Maria I. Stewart, all of Burlington, N.J. At Allentown N.J., April 28, by Rev. Peter Gardiner, Cato Dubois to Miss Edith Parker. On the evening of April 25, by Rev. J. B. Reeve, Mr. Amos B. Seynes [VERIFY] to Miss Mary B., daughter of James Clay [VERIFY] Esq.

articles.headline: Deaths
articles.summary: Eliza A. Butler, aged 45, died April 29, 1867; funeral from her husband's residence, No. 737 Kaighn's Point Avenue, Camden N.J., Saturday May 4 at 1 p.m. Rachel Wilkins died April 24, 1867, Camden N.J., of typhoid, consort of Daniel Wilkins, in her 55th year. Also an obituary of Louisa Hill of Wilmington, Del. (text only).

articles.summary: Sheba Lodge, Juvenile I. O. of Good Samaritans and D. of Samaria, meets 2d Thursday of each month at 2 o'clock P.M. at Masonic Hall, South Eleventh Street; A. Cropper, F. O.; S. O. of Good Samaritans and Daughters of Samaria, meets second and fourth Thursdays each month at Masonic Hall, South Eleventh Street, Philadelphia, at 8 o'clock (apr 6 '67 1y).
people: F. O., Sheba Lodge (Juvenile Good Samaritans)

events.name: Sarah's Tent (benevolent female organization) -- anniversary
events.description: Sarah's Tent, a benevolent female organization, held its anniversary on the 18th of last month (April 18, 1867) at Masonic Hall. Speeches by Mrs. Howard, Revs. Smith, Kinnard and Lynch, and Mr. Larence [VERIFY]. Surname-only speakers kept in text.

events.name: Colored People's Union League -- Grand Reunion Festival
events.description: PHILADELPHIA AFFAIRS: The Grand Reunion Festival of the Colored People's Union League was held on the 20th ultimo; reported by Mr. A. M. Green; eloquent speeches. Committee of Arrangements: Guy M. Burton, Thos. J. Bowers, Andrew F. Stevens, Jesse E. Glasgow, James W. Brown, Rev. Stephen Smith, Joshua D. Kelley, Benjamin Harrison, Thomas H. Davis, G. W. Gaines [VERIFY] and John C. Bowers.

events.name: Serenade to Hon. John W. Forney by colored citizens
events.description: On the evening of the 26th ultimo a delegation of colored citizens serenaded the Hon. John W. Forney at his residence, with a celebrated colored band, on the eve of his sailing for Europe. Address by O. V. Catto, Esq. (Parade/procession topic.)

events.name: Complimentary concert to Mr. A. Harris [VERIFY]
events.description: A complimentary concert to Mr. A. Harris [VERIFY surname], the renowned musician, at Liberty Hall last Monday evening (April 29). (Liberty Hall topic.)

events.name: Love feast at Bethel A.M.E. Church
events.location: Bethel A.M.E. Church, Sixth St., Philadelphia
events.description: Love feast at Bethel (Rev. James Hollen, pastor) Monday night last (April 29); itinerant ministers present included Revs. Mitchell, Gibbs, Weaver, Gould and James Lynch.

events.description: Notice: the fourth quarterly meeting of Union A.M.E. Church, Coates street, Sunday May 5, 1867. Ministers expected: Rev. Mr. Carr of Charleston S.C., Rev. T. H. Turpin, Rev. Elisha Weaver, Rev. W. D. W. Schureman. R. P. Gibbs, pastor [VERIFY, print blurred]. Dated April 29.
